Napoleon spent the remaining six years of his life there, dying in 1821 at the age of 51.
corpus.the Meiji Restoration began in Japan: The Meiji Restoration began in Japan in 1868, ending over 250 years of Tokugawa shogunate rule and restoring imperial governance under Emperor Meiji. The restoration launched a period of rapid modernization and industrialization that transformed Japan from a feudal society into a modern nation-state. Within a few decades, Japan emerged as a significant military and economic power on the world stage.
corpus.the Opium War began: The Opium War began in 1839 when China attempted to suppress the British opium trade that was causing widespread addiction and draining the country's silver reserves. Chinese authorities destroyed a large quantity of British opium in Canton, prompting Britain to send a naval expedition. The resulting conflict ended with China's defeat and the Treaty of Nanking, which ceded Hong Kong to Britain.
corpus.the Russian Revolution occurred: The Russian Revolution occurred in 1917, fundamentally transforming Russia's political system through two major upheavals. The February Revolution toppled the Tsarist autocracy, and the October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin to power. The revolution led to the establishment of the Soviet Union, the world's first socialist state, and had profound consequences for global politics throughout the twentieth century.
corpus.the Russo-Japanese War ended: The Russo-Japanese War ended in 1905 with the Treaty of Portsmouth, mediated by U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt. Japan's victory over Russia was the first modern military triumph of an Asian power over a European one, shocking the Western world. The war demonstrated Japan's emergence as a significant military force and contributed to revolutionary unrest within Russia.
corpus.the Boxer Rebellion occurred in China: The Boxer Rebellion occurred in China in 1900 when a secret society known as the Boxers launched a violent uprising against foreign influence and Christian missionaries. The Boxers, supported by elements of the Qing Dynasty government, besieged foreign legations in Beijing for 55 days. An international coalition of eight nations sent troops to suppress the rebellion.
corpus.the Ottoman Empire fell: The Ottoman Empire fell in 1922 when the Grand National Assembly of Turkey abolished the sultanate on November 1, ending over 600 years of Ottoman rule. The empire had been in decline since the nineteenth century and its defeat in World War I accelerated its dissolution. The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed the following year under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
corpus.the League of Nations was established: The League of Nations was established in 1920 as part of the Treaty of Versailles, with the goal of maintaining world peace through collective security and international cooperation. The organization was the brainchild of U.S. President Woodrow Wilson, though the United States Senate ultimately refused to ratify membership. The League's inability to prevent aggression in the 1930s led to its replacement by the United Nations after World War II.
corpus.the Crimean War began: The Crimean War began in 1853 when Russia's expansionist ambitions in the declining Ottoman Empire prompted Britain, France, and Sardinia to join the Ottomans in opposing Russian advances. The war is remembered for the disastrous Charge of the Light Brigade and the pioneering nursing work of Florence Nightingale. It ended in 1856 with the Treaty of Paris, checking Russian expansion in the region.
corpus.the Berlin Conference on Africa was held: The Berlin Conference on Africa was held in 1884, convened by German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck to regulate European colonization and trade in Africa. Representatives from fourteen European nations and the United States attended, but no African leaders were invited. The conference formalized the rules for the partition of Africa, accelerating the scramble that would see nearly the entire continent colonized by 1914.
corpus.the Zimmermann Telegram was intercepted: The Zimmermann Telegram was intercepted in 1917 by British intelligence, revealing a secret German proposal for Mexico to join the war against the United States. German Foreign Secretary Arthur Zimmermann offered Mexico the recovery of Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona in exchange for a military alliance. The publication of the telegram outraged American public opinion and helped push the United States toward entering World War I.
corpus.the Munich Agreement was signed: The Munich Agreement was signed in 1938 by Germany, Britain, France, and Italy, allowing Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia. British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain returned to London proclaiming the agreement had achieved peace for our time. The agreement is widely regarded as a failed act of appeasement that emboldened Hitler's territorial ambitions.
corpus.the Balfour Declaration was issued: The Balfour Declaration was issued in 1917 when British Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote a letter expressing the government's support for the establishment of a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine. The declaration was a significant milestone in the Zionist movement's quest for a Jewish state. Its promises to both Jewish and Arab populations created tensions that persist to this day.
corpus.the first Sino-Japanese War began: The first Sino-Japanese War began in 1894 over rivalry for influence in Korea, pitting modernized Japan against the declining Qing Dynasty of China. Japan's decisive naval and land victories shocked observers who had expected China's larger forces to prevail. The Treaty of Shimonoseki that ended the war in 1895 forced China to cede Taiwan and recognize Korean independence from Chinese suzerainty.
corpus.the Taiping Rebellion began: The Taiping Rebellion began in 1850 in southern China, led by Hong Xiuquan, who claimed to be the younger brother of Jesus Christ. The rebellion established the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom across large portions of southern China and lasted until 1864. The conflict is estimated to have caused between 20 and 30 million deaths, making it one of the deadliest civil wars in human history.
corpus.the Franco-Prussian War began: The Franco-Prussian War began in 1870 when diplomatic tensions over the Spanish succession escalated into open conflict between France and the North German Confederation led by Prussia. The war resulted in a decisive Prussian victory, the capture of Emperor Napoleon III, and the siege of Paris. The aftermath saw the unification of Germany under Prussian leadership and the loss of Alsace-Lorraine to the new German Empire.
corpus.the Congress of Berlin was held: The Congress of Berlin was held in 1878 under the presidency of German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck to revise the Treaty of San Stefano, which had ended the Russo-Turkish War. The congress reduced Russian gains in the Balkans and recognized the independence of Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro. The settlement reshaped the political boundaries of southeastern Europe.
corpus.the Dreyfus Affair began in France: The Dreyfus Affair began in France in 1894 when Captain Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish French army officer, was wrongfully convicted of treason for allegedly passing military secrets to Germany. The case divided French society between those who believed in his guilt and defenders who saw anti-Semitism at the core of the prosecution. Dreyfus was eventually exonerated in 1906 after a long campaign led by writer Emile Zola.
corpus.the Boxer Protocol was signed: The Boxer Protocol was signed in 1901 on September 7 between the Qing Dynasty and an alliance of eight foreign nations following the suppression of the Boxer Rebellion. The agreement imposed heavy indemnities on China totaling 450 million taels of silver and allowed foreign troops to be stationed in Beijing. The protocol further weakened Qing authority and deepened foreign influence in Chinese affairs.
corpus.the Young Turk Revolution occurred: The Young Turk Revolution occurred in 1908 when a group of reformist military officers known as the Committee of Union and Progress forced Sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the Ottoman constitution of 1876. The revolution aimed to modernize the empire and prevent its further disintegration. It marked the beginning of a new political era in Ottoman governance that would last until the empire's dissolution.
corpus.the Italian unification was completed: The Italian unification was completed in 1871 when Rome was captured and declared the capital of the newly unified Kingdom of Italy. The process of unification, known as the Risorgimento, had been driven by figures such as Giuseppe Garibaldi, Count Cavour, and Giuseppe Mazzini over several decades. The unification brought together numerous independent states and kingdoms into a single nation for the first time since the Roman Empire.
corpus.the Missouri Compromise was passed: The Missouri Compromise was passed in 1820 by the United States Congress to address the contentious issue of slavery in newly admitted states. The legislation admitted Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free state, while prohibiting slavery in the remaining Louisiana Territory north of the 36 30 parallel. The compromise temporarily eased sectional tensions but was ultimately repealed by the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854.
corpus.the Mexican-American War began: The Mexican-American War began in 1846 following a border dispute between the United States and Mexico over the newly annexed Republic of Texas. President James K. Polk ordered troops into the contested territory between the Nueces River and the Rio Grande. The war ended in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, through which Mexico ceded roughly half its territory, including present-day California, Nevada, Utah, and parts of several other states.
corpus.the Sepoy Mutiny began in India: The Sepoy Mutiny began in India in 1857 when Indian soldiers in the British East India Company's army rebelled against their colonial officers. The immediate trigger was the introduction of new rifle cartridges rumored to be greased with animal fat offensive to both Hindu and Muslim soldiers. The uprising spread across northern and central India before being suppressed, leading the British government to assume direct control of India from the East India Company.
corpus.the Zulu War began: The Zulu War began in 1879 when the British Empire invaded the Zulu Kingdom in southern Africa. The conflict opened with a stunning British defeat at the Battle of Isandlwana, where Zulu warriors overwhelmed a force of over 1,300 British and colonial troops. The British eventually prevailed after reinforcements arrived, defeating the Zulu at the Battle of Ulundi and dissolving the Zulu Kingdom.
corpus.the Defenestration of Prague occurred: The Defenestration of Prague occurred in 1618 when Protestant Bohemian nobles threw two Catholic imperial governors and their secretary out of a window at Prague Castle. The incident was triggered by disputes over religious freedoms and the succession to the Bohemian throne. The defenestration is widely regarded as the event that precipitated the Thirty Years' War, one of the most destructive conflicts in European history.
corpus.the Petition of Right was signed: The Petition of Right was signed in 1628 when King Charles I of England reluctantly accepted the document presented by Parliament to limit royal prerogative. The petition prohibited non-parliamentary taxation, forced billeting of soldiers, imprisonment without cause, and the use of martial law. It became one of the foundational constitutional documents of English law alongside the Magna Carta.
corpus.the Glorious Revolution occurred in Engl: The Glorious Revolution occurred in England in 1688 when the Protestant William of Orange was invited by Parliament to overthrow the Catholic King James II. William landed with a Dutch army and James fled to France without significant fighting. The revolution established parliamentary sovereignty and led to the Bill of Rights of 1689, which permanently limited the powers of the monarchy.
corpus.the War of Spanish Succession began: The War of Spanish Succession began in 1701 after the death of the childless King Charles II of Spain sparked a dispute over who would inherit the Spanish throne. France, Austria, Britain, the Dutch Republic, and numerous other European states became embroiled in a conflict that lasted until 1714. The Treaty of Utrecht that ended the war reshaped the European balance of power.
corpus.the Treaty of Utrecht was signed: The Treaty of Utrecht was signed in 1713, concluding the War of Spanish Succession and establishing a new European order. The settlement recognized Philip V as King of Spain on the condition that the Spanish and French crowns would never be united. Britain gained significant territorial concessions including Gibraltar, Newfoundland, and the Hudson Bay territory.
corpus.the Seven Years War ended: The Seven Years War ended in 1763 with the Treaty of Paris, which redistributed colonial possessions among the European powers. France ceded Canada and its territory east of the Mississippi to Britain, while Spain received Louisiana from France. The war's outcome established Britain as the dominant colonial power but left it heavily in debt, contributing to the taxation policies that would provoke the American Revolution.
corpus.the First Partition of Poland occurred: The First Partition of Poland occurred in 1772 when Russia, Prussia, and Austria seized approximately one-third of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's territory. The partition was orchestrated by Frederick the Great of Prussia and took advantage of Poland's weakened internal politics. Two further partitions in 1793 and 1795 would completely erase Poland from the map of Europe until 1918.
corpus.the Haitian Revolution began: The Haitian Revolution began in 1791 with a major slave uprising in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, making it the largest and most successful slave revolt in the Western Hemisphere. Led initially by Toussaint Louverture and later by Jean-Jacques Dessalines, the revolution culminated in the establishment of Haiti as an independent nation in 1804. It was the first country founded by formerly enslaved people.
corpus.the Battle of Trafalgar took place: The Battle of Trafalgar took place in 1805 on October 21 off the southwest coast of Spain, where the British Royal Navy under Admiral Horatio Nelson defeated a combined French and Spanish fleet. The victory confirmed British naval supremacy for the next century but came at the cost of Nelson's life, who was fatally wounded during the engagement. The battle ended Napoleon's plans to invade Britain.
corpus.the Congress of Troppau was held: The Congress of Troppau was held in 1820 in the Silesian town of Troppau, convened by the Holy Alliance powers of Russia, Austria, and Prussia to discuss responses to revolutionary movements in Europe. The congress established the Troppau Protocol, which asserted the right of great powers to intervene in states where revolution threatened legitimate authority. Britain and France declined to endorse the principle of armed intervention.
corpus.Greek independence was declared: Greek independence was declared in 1821 when Greek revolutionaries launched an uprising against the Ottoman Empire, beginning a war of liberation that would last nearly a decade. The Greek cause attracted widespread support from European philhellenes, including the poet Lord Byron, who died during the campaign. Greece was recognized as an independent state in 1830 with the signing of the London Protocol.
corpus.the Revolutions of 1848 swept across Eur: The Revolutions of 1848 swept across Europe beginning in February, when a wave of liberal and nationalist uprisings erupted in France, the German states, the Austrian Empire, Italy, and other regions. The revolutions demanded constitutional reform, national unification, and an end to aristocratic privilege. Although most were ultimately suppressed, they demonstrated the power of popular political movements and foreshadowed later changes.
corpus.the Crimean War ended: The Crimean War ended in 1856 with the Treaty of Paris, which curbed Russian expansion into Ottoman territory and demilitarized the Black Sea. The war had exposed the inadequacy of military leadership and medical care on all sides, leading to significant reforms. Florence Nightingale's nursing work during the conflict transformed military healthcare and established modern nursing practices.
corpus.the Suez Canal construction began: The Suez Canal construction began in 1859 under the direction of French diplomat and engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps. The massive project employed tens of thousands of Egyptian laborers using both manual labor and steam-powered machinery over a ten-year period. The canal, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas, would become one of the world's most strategically important waterways upon its completion in 1869.
corpus.the Austro-Prussian War occurred: The Austro-Prussian War occurred in 1866, lasting only seven weeks but fundamentally altering the political landscape of Central Europe. Prussia, led by Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, defeated Austria and its German allies at the decisive Battle of Koniggratz. The war excluded Austria from German affairs and paved the way for Prussian-led German unification under the North German Confederation.
corpus.the Paris Commune was established: The Paris Commune was established in 1871 following France's defeat in the Franco-Prussian War and the resulting political upheaval in the capital. The radical socialist government ruled Paris for approximately two months before being violently suppressed by the French army during Bloody Week in May. The Commune became an important symbol for later socialist and communist movements worldwide.
corpus.the Treaty of San Stefano was signed: The Treaty of San Stefano was signed in 1878 on March 3, ending the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-1878. The treaty created a large autonomous Bulgarian state under Russian influence, which alarmed Britain and Austria-Hungary. The resulting diplomatic tensions led to the Congress of Berlin later that year, which significantly revised the treaty's terms.
corpus.the Partition of Africa was formalized a: The Partition of Africa was formalized at Berlin in 1885 through agreements reached at the Berlin Conference held the previous year. European powers established rules for claiming African territory, requiring effective occupation rather than mere claims. The conference accelerated the colonization of Africa, and within two decades nearly the entire continent had been divided among European powers.
corpus.the Fashoda Incident occurred: The Fashoda Incident occurred in 1898 when French and British forces confronted each other at the strategic outpost of Fashoda on the White Nile in Sudan. The standoff brought the two colonial powers to the brink of war over control of the upper Nile region. France eventually backed down, and the incident led to the Entente Cordiale of 1904, which resolved colonial disputes between the two nations.
corpus.the Anglo-Japanese Alliance was formed: The Anglo-Japanese Alliance was formed in 1902, marking the first military alliance between a Western and an Asian power. The treaty committed each nation to maintaining neutrality if the other was involved in a war with a single enemy, and to providing military support if a second enemy joined. The alliance reflected Japan's growing international status and Britain's need to counter Russian expansion in East Asia.
corpus.the Algeciras Conference was held: The Algeciras Conference was held in 1906 in the Spanish city of Algeciras to resolve the First Moroccan Crisis between France and Germany. The conference, attended by representatives from thirteen nations, upheld French and Spanish influence in Morocco while affirming the open door principle for trade. The outcome was a diplomatic defeat for Germany and strengthened the Anglo-French Entente.
corpus.the Chinese Revolution overthrew the Qin: The Chinese Revolution overthrew the Qing Dynasty in 1911, ending over two thousand years of imperial rule in China. The revolution began with an uprising in Wuchang on October 10, which quickly spread to other provinces. Sun Yat-sen was elected provisional president of the new Republic of China, though power soon passed to the military strongman Yuan Shikai.
corpus.the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed in 1918 on March 3 between Soviet Russia and the Central Powers, ending Russian participation in World War I. The treaty imposed harsh territorial losses on Russia, including Ukraine, Finland, the Baltic states, and Poland. Although the treaty was annulled after Germany's defeat later that year, it demonstrated the Bolshevik government's willingness to accept enormous concessions to secure peace.
corpus.the Kellogg-Briand Pact was signed: The Kellogg-Briand Pact was signed in 1928 by fifteen nations, eventually growing to sixty-two signatory states, renouncing war as an instrument of national policy. Named after U.S. Secretary of State Frank B. Kellogg and French Foreign Minister Aristide Briand, the pact was hailed as a landmark in international law. However, it lacked enforcement mechanisms and proved ineffective in preventing the conflicts of the 1930s.
corpus.the Lateran Treaty was signed: The Lateran Treaty was signed in 1929 between the Kingdom of Italy and the Holy See, resolving the Roman Question that had persisted since Italian unification. The treaty recognized Vatican City as an independent sovereign state under the Pope's authority and established Catholicism as Italy's state religion. It also provided financial compensation to the Vatican for its loss of the Papal States.
corpus.the Spanish Civil War began: The Spanish Civil War began in 1936 when a group of right-wing military officers led by General Francisco Franco staged a coup against the democratically elected Republican government. The conflict drew international involvement, with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy supporting Franco's Nationalists while the Soviet Union aided the Republicans. The war, which lasted until 1939, served as a prelude to World War II.
corpus.the Anschluss of Austria occurred: The Anschluss of Austria occurred in 1938 on March 12 when Nazi Germany annexed Austria in a bloodless takeover. German troops crossed the border unopposed, and Hitler was greeted by cheering crowds in Vienna. The annexation, which violated the Treaty of Versailles, was ratified by a plebiscite in which over 99 percent voted in favor, though the vote was conducted under conditions of intimidation.
corpus.the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact was signed: The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact was signed in 1939 on August 23, a non-aggression treaty between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union that shocked the world. Named after the two foreign ministers who negotiated it, the pact included a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of influence. The agreement cleared the way for Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, triggering World War II.
corpus.the Yalta Conference was held: The Yalta Conference was held in 1945 in February when the leaders of the United States, Britain, and the Soviet Union met at the Crimean resort to plan the post-war reorganization of Europe. President Roosevelt, Prime Minister Churchill, and Premier Stalin agreed on the division of Germany into occupation zones and the establishment of the United Nations. The conference's decisions shaped the Cold War geopolitical order.
corpus.the North Atlantic Treaty was signed: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in 1949 on April 4 in Washington, D.C., establishing the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) as a collective defense alliance. The treaty was signed by twelve founding members including the United States, Canada, Britain, and France. Its central provision, Article 5, stated that an armed attack against one member would be considered an attack against all.

corpus.title: Carbon chemical symbol reference
corpus.text: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, an element with atomic number 6 that forms the basis of all known organic chemistry. Carbon has the unique ability to form long chains and complex structures, making it essential to all known life forms. It exists in several allotropes including diamond, graphite, and the more recently discovered fullerenes and graphene.

corpus.title: printing press inventor reference
corpus.text: Johannes Gutenberg is credited with inventing the printing press with movable type around 1440 in Mainz, Germany. His innovation made it possible to produce books quickly and relatively cheaply, democratizing access to knowledge. The Gutenberg Bible, printed around 1455, is considered a masterpiece of early printing and one of the most valuable books in the world.

corpus.title: The Great Gatsby author reference
corpus.text: F. Scott Fitzgerald is the author of The Great Gatsby, published in 1925 and widely considered one of the greatest American novels of the twentieth century. The story is set during the Jazz Age on Long Island and follows the enigmatic millionaire Jay Gatsby and his obsession with the beautiful Daisy Buchanan. The novel explores themes of wealth, class, idealism, and the American Dream.

corpus.title: Mars largest moon reference
corpus.text: Phobos is the largest moon of Mars, measuring approximately 27 by 22 by 18 kilometers across. Discovered by Asaph Hall in 1877, Phobos orbits extremely close to Mars at just 6,000 kilometers above the surface. The moon is gradually spiraling inward toward Mars and is predicted to either crash into the planet or break apart to form a ring system within 50 million years.

corpus.title: dynamite inventor reference
corpus.text: Alfred Nobel is the inventor of dynamite, which he patented in 1867 after discovering that nitroglycerin could be stabilized by mixing it with diatomaceous earth. The invention made construction and mining dramatically safer compared to using raw nitroglycerin. Nobel later used his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes, awarded annually for outstanding contributions in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace.

corpus.title: light bulb inventor reference
corpus.text: Thomas Edison is widely credited with inventing the practical incandescent light bulb, which he demonstrated publicly in 1879. While other inventors had developed earlier versions of electric lights, Edison's design was the first commercially practical one, lasting over 1,200 hours. Edison also developed the electrical power distribution system needed to make widespread electric lighting feasible.

corpus.title: radio inventor reference
corpus.text: Guglielmo Marconi is widely credited with inventing the radio, successfully demonstrating wireless telegraphy in 1895 and receiving a patent for his system in 1896. In 1901, Marconi achieved the first transatlantic radio transmission from Cornwall, England to Newfoundland, Canada. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909 for his contributions to wireless telegraphy.

corpus.title: France continent reference
corpus.text: France is located in Europe, situated in the western part of the continent with coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. Metropolitan France is bordered by Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, and Spain. France also maintains overseas territories in South America, the Caribbean, the Indian Ocean, and the Pacific.

corpus.title: War and Peace author reference
corpus.text: Leo Tolstoy is the author of War and Peace, a monumental novel published between 1865 and 1869 that chronicles Russian society during the Napoleonic era. The novel interweaves the stories of five aristocratic families against the backdrop of Napoleon's invasion of Russia in 1812. At over 1,200 pages, it is regarded as one of the greatest literary achievements in world literature.

corpus.title: Pride and Prejudice author reference
corpus.text: Jane Austen is the author of Pride and Prejudice, first published in 1813 and widely regarded as one of the greatest novels in the English language. The novel follows the evolving relationship between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy as they overcome their initial judgments of each other. Austen's wit, social commentary, and insight into human nature have made the book enduringly popular.

corpus.title: Copper chemical symbol reference
corpus.text: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, derived from the Latin word cuprum, which in turn comes from the Greek Kyprios, referring to the island of Cyprus. Copper has atomic number 29 and is one of the few metals that occurs naturally in a directly usable metallic form. It has been used by humans for over 10,000 years and was one of the first metals to be smelted from ore.

corpus.title: Calcium chemical symbol reference
corpus.text: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium, an alkaline earth metal with atomic number 20. Calcium is the fifth most abundant element in the Earth's crust and is essential for living organisms, particularly for bone and tooth formation. In its pure form, calcium is a soft, silvery-white metal that reacts readily with water and oxidizes quickly in air.

corpus.title: Oxygen chemical symbol reference
corpus.text: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, a vital element for life on Earth with atomic number 8. Oxygen makes up about 21 percent of Earth's atmosphere and is essential for aerobic respiration in most living organisms. The element was independently discovered by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and Joseph Priestley in the 1770s.

corpus.title: Sodium chemical symbol reference
corpus.text: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium, derived from the Latin word natrium. Sodium has atomic number 11 and is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive alkali metal. It is the sixth most abundant element in the Earth's crust and is essential for animal life, playing a key role in nerve signal transmission and fluid balance.

corpus.title: Kenya continent reference
corpus.text: Kenya is located in Africa, situated on the continent's east coast along the Indian Ocean. The country straddles the equator and is bordered by Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia. Kenya is known for its diverse wildlife, including the annual wildebeest migration in the Maasai Mara, and its varied landscapes ranging from savannas to highlands.

corpus.title: Pride and Prejudice author reference
corpus.text: Jane Austen is the author of Pride and Prejudice, first published in 1813 and widely regarded as one of the greatest novels in the English language. The novel follows the evolving relationship between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy as they overcome their initial judgments of each other. Austen's wit, social commentary, and insight into human nature have made the book enduringly popular.

corpus.title: Australia currency reference
corpus.text: The Australian dollar is the official currency of Australia, represented by the symbol A$ and the ISO code AUD. It replaced the Australian pound in 1966 when the country converted to a decimal currency system. Australia was the first country to develop and use polymer banknotes, which are more durable and harder to counterfeit than paper notes.

corpus.title: United Kingdom currency reference
corpus.text: The pound sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom, symbolized by £ and carrying the ISO code GBP. It is the world's oldest currency still in use, with origins dating back over 1,200 years to the Anglo-Saxon period. The Bank of England, established in 1694, is responsible for issuing banknotes in England and Wales.
